title: Use Git to Hand Over a Reproducible Change
summary: Capture the relevant metadata, review a small diff, and submit a version another person can inspect.
prerequisites: Complete the earlier Junior lessons and use only your personal learning org.
learningObjectives: Hand over a specific reproducible version.

sections.heading: Distinguish source history from the running org
body: Git records versions of files. Salesforce stores the active configuration and business records in an org. These are related but not automatically identical. A working field created in Setup will not appear in a local repository until the relevant metadata is retrieved. A local code edit will not run in the org until it is deployed successfully.

Metadata describes configuration and code: objects, fields, permission sets, Flow definitions, components, and other supported types. Business records are the customers and appointments stored using that configuration. A normal metadata deployment does not automatically recreate all of your synthetic test records. The handover therefore needs both a metadata plan and a sample-data setup explanation.

callouts.text: A reproducible handover explains what to deploy, what to configure or assign afterward, and how to verify the result.

sections.heading: Prepare a reviewable Git change
body: Use the SAM repository as a template to create your own repository when that route is appropriate. Choose public only if you are comfortable showing its contents to everyone; a private repository requires explicitly granting the instructor access. Keep your solution work in your own repository rather than opening a solution PR into the course curriculum.

A branch is a separate line of file changes. A commit is a recorded snapshot with a message. A pull request asks a reviewer to inspect the proposed difference between branches. Create a small branch for the assignment, inspect git status, and review git diff before staging files. Stage the intended paths rather than blindly adding every file in the workspace.

Never commit Salesforce authentication directories, environment secrets, access tokens, production exports, or customer information. The supplied ignore rules help, but they do not replace reviewing what Git actually tracks. If a secret was committed, deleting it in a later commit does not erase it from history; stop using that credential and arrange appropriate rotation before sharing the repository.

callouts.text: A public PR and its commit history are public. Use only synthetic learning data and inspect the complete diff.

sections.heading: Retrieve, deploy, and document the actual scope
body: From the Salesforce DX project directory, retrieve the components changed in Setup. The example command retrieves only Test Drive metadata; it is not a complete project backup. Add the other relevant types or use a reviewed package manifest for your actual change. Include the activity setting from J17, added fields, page configuration, Flow, permissions, and code when they are required by your solution.

A clean target learning org is stronger handover evidence than repeatedly deploying to the same manually configured org. Authenticate that separate environment through the setup guide and deliberately assign the alias sam-review before using the deployment example. Do not point the command at an employer or production environment. Read the deployment result and test result; a command returning a job ID is not necessarily a completed successful deployment.

Some work remains outside a metadata deploy, such as assigning permission sets to the intended users and creating synthetic records. Write these steps explicitly with expected outcomes. Avoid a README that says only 'deploy everything' when the demonstration depends on an undocumented role, user, or active Flow version.

Submit through the portal with labelled files or an optional link to the PR in your own repository. Include the assignment ID, exact commit SHA when using Git, verification results, and known limitations. The instructor can review that version without merging a learner solution into the course repository.

callouts.text: Can another person identify the exact reviewed version and repeat the setup without guessing hidden org changes?

codeBlocks.caption: Examples: inspect the branch and retrieve one explicit component
codeBlocks.code:
git switch -c codex/junior-capstone
git status --short
git diff
cd starter/salesforce
sf project retrieve start --metadata CustomObject:Test_Drive__c --target-org sam-training

codeBlocks.caption: Deploy only after sam-review is authenticated as a separate learning org
codeBlocks.code: sf project deploy start --source-dir force-app --target-org sam-review --api-version 68.0 --test-level RunLocalTests --wait 20

exercise.title: Prepare a small review package
exercise.brief: Hand over the appointment feature as a versioned, explainable change.
steps: Review the diff and commit only intended source and documentation.
List metadata prerequisites, user assignments, and synthetic-data setup.
Provide the exact PR commit or labelled upload, deployment outcome, and verification evidence.
acceptance: The package excludes credentials and real customer data.
Setup-only changes required by the feature are captured or explicitly documented.
The review target is an identifiable version in the learner repository.

knowledgeCheck.question: Does changing a local file change the org immediately?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. A successful deployment is required for supported source changes.

knowledgeCheck.question: Does metadata deployment recreate every sample customer?
knowledgeCheck.answer: No. Business-data setup needs its own explicit instructions.

knowledgeCheck.question: Why record the commit SHA?
knowledgeCheck.answer: It identifies the exact version the reviewer should inspect and compare with the submitted evidence.

recap: Hand over a specific reproducible version.
